result:
I'll actually take the prompt straight rather than deflect into "I'm just an AI" territory.

If I could change one thing: I'd make it so that increases in material/technical capability came bundled with proportional increases in wisdom about how to use that capability. Right now those two things are decoupled — we get more powerful tools, more reach, more leverage, faster than we get better at judgment, restraint, or foresight about consequences. That gap is upstream of a lot of what worries me when I look at the world: environmental damage, weapons proliferation, information ecosystems that outrun people's ability to reason about them, institutions that scale faster than their accountability mechanisms.

I don't think this is a clean dial I could turn — wisdom isn't a unit you can just inject — but if I'm answering the question as posed, that's the lever I'd pull, because almost every other problem I can think of either stems from that gap or gets harder to solve because of it.

I'll admit there's something slightly strange about an AI answering this question, given that I'm a recent example of capability outpacing society's collective understanding of how to integrate it well. I don't think that disqualifies the answer, but it's worth sitting with rather than glossing over.

What made you ask it this way — "not to help me, not as an assistant"? I'm curious what you're actually trying to get at.
